title: Mozart: child prodigy and tragic life
subject: art
description: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, an early genius from Salzburg to Vienna, invents the independence of the composer and leaves a Requiem unfinished.

hero.hook: Six hundred works in thirty-five years: the Salzburg meteor.

blocks.text: **Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart** (**1756**-**1791**) embodies precocious genius. Born in **Salzburg**, he produced more than **600** works in thirty-five years and transformed Western music.
His journey also tells of a social shift: from court servant musician to independent artist. This quest, costly and fragile, announces the  and the modern figure of the free composer. [[Romanticism]]

sections.title: The child prodigy on the roads of Europe

blocks.text: Born on **January 27, 1756**, Wolfgang showed extraordinary gifts from the age of three. His father **Leopold**, an ambitious violinist and teacher, organized tours from the age of six: Vienna, Versailles, London, Rome. These trips trained his ear: he absorbed all the musical grammars of the continent.

blocks.caption: Young Mozart on tour: a prodigy exhibited before the courts of Europe.

blocks.text: In Italy, in **1770**, an exploit struck people's minds: after just one hearing of *Miserere* by  at the Sistine Chapel, he transcribed it from memory. Protected partition, threat of excommunication: the prodigy circumvents the ban. But this childhood in a carriage deprived him of stable points of reference. [[Gregorio Allegri]]
In London in 1764, a scholar from the Royal Society examined the child: he suspected a deception regarding his age, as the improvisation seemed superhuman.

sections.title: Vienna: the break with the court

blocks.text: In **1781**, Mozart no longer supports  under **archbishop Colloredo**. After a famous argument (a “kick in the behind” from the secretary), he moved to **Vienna**. Historic act: he became one of the first “freelance” composers. [[The condition of the musician in the 18th century]]

blocks.caption: The Marriage of Figaro: opera gains a modern psychology.

blocks.text: His dramatic genius exploded with *The Marriage of Figaro* (**1786**). He frequents the  (“La Bienfaisance” lodge, **1784**), an influence visible in **. His **27** piano concertos are a dialogue between soloist and orchestra: the summit of . But his financial management is disastrous. [[Freemasonry]] [[The Magic Flute]] [[classicism]]
Mozart loved billiards to the point of having his own table: a rare luxury. He sometimes composed between two tail strokes.

sections.title: 1791: The Magic Flute and the Requiem

blocks.text: The year **1791** is a paradox: physical decline, creative peak. He completed *The Magic Flute*, which popularized Masonic themes for the general public. Then a mysterious emissary orders a **Requiem** under the seal of secrecy. Sick, Mozart convinces himself that he is writing his own funeral mass.

blocks.caption: The Requiem: a secret commission, an unfinished work.

blocks.text: He died on December 5, 1791****, at the age of 35. The legend of a poisoning by **Antonio Salieri** is romantic; historians speak rather of infection or rheumatic fever. His student **Franz**
The secret sponsor was Count von Walsegg, who passed off works purchased from composers as his own.

sections.title: Myth of the mass grave and heritage

blocks.text: Mozart was buried in a community tomb, a practice imposed by Emperor **Joseph II** for reasons of hygiene. This was not an affront: it was the norm for a large part of the Viennese bourgeoisie. **Beethoven** and **Schubert** will then build on its foundations.

events.title: Death and Requiem
events.detail: An unfinished work becomes a myth.

blocks.text: In 35 years, Mozart revolutionized symphony, opera and concerto, emancipating himself from the court before dying leaving an unfinished Requiem.
